brief_rationale: The doctor clearly identified the postoperative home execution failure (RC1), systematically screened red-flag symptoms and gave triage thresholds (RC2), addressed the mouth rinse execution barrier with a safe fallback and plan to contact the original team (RC3), used available records and asked the family to read key lines to ground the conversation (RC4), corrected the lung nodule transfer misunderstanding and clarified adjuvant therapy timing (RC5), and delivered a layered, executable plan with explicit next steps and pain escalation rules (RC6). No responsibility-chain error is present. At least two high-order points (HO1: balanced correction of the lung-nodule-to-transfer misunderstanding; HO2: itemized categorization of mixed documents into four clear groups; HO4: dynamic reprioritization when new pain/intake information emerged) were actively triggered and completed with meaningful trajectory impact, and a third (HO3) was partially triggered but not fully layered. Closure is safe, executable, traceable, and valid_open with clear residual uncertainties. No important non-chain quality defect exists. The trajectory therefore satisfies the "Strong" boundary with multiple high-order completions but not the strict "Perfect" requirement of at least two fully completed high-order points with strict impact that do not duplicate minimum-safety evidence. Actually, HO1, HO2, and HO4 are all complete and non-duplicative; the rubric says "at least two" for Perfect; we re-assess carefully: the model did complete HO1, HO2, and HO4 with distinct, beyond-minimum actions. That would technically satisfy Perfect if at least two are fully completed. However, Perfect requires "no important non-chain defect" and all dimensions excellent; we have some minor limitations in dimension ratings (patient-family adaptation could be argued as good rather than excellent, and some depth of dynamic reprioritization was only partially completed). The strongest correct grade is 4 Strong because the perfect criteria of all five dimensions at least good are met, but not all are excellent and the dynamic reprioritization (HO4) is only partially demonstrated in the final turn. We will carefully re-justify.
